findings.text: Early startup helper installs a named directory as the current working directory. It resolves the name with link following and directory requirements, verifies execute and directory change access, records the location as the process working directory only on success, always releases the looked up reference, and reports the first encountered failure.

Early startup helper installs a named directory as the filesystem root. It resolves the name with link following and directory requirements, verifies execute and directory change access, demands chroot privilege in the current user context, consults security policy for the transition, switches the root only after all approvals, always releases the reference, and reports status.

Early startup helper changes ownership of a named object. Link following is suppressed only when nofollow is requested. It acquires a write hold on the containing mount while shared ownership logic runs, then drops the mount hold and path reference and reports status.

Early helpers for mode update, accessibility probe and status fetch each resolve a name then delegate. Mode update follows links and uses shared mode logic. Accessibility probe follows links and checks access rights. Status fetch optionally follows links, disables automount during the query, requests basic statistics, fills caller storage, and releases the reference in each case.

Early helpers for special node creation and hardlink creation wrap filename oriented dispatch with default directory descriptors. Node creation forwards caller mode and device encoding to shared mknod handling. Link creation forwards old and new names with no additional options to shared link handling. Both translate textual names through kernel filename objects.

Shared ownership update converts caller user and group values into kernel identities, builds an attribute set marking time update with optional owner and group entries, rejects invalid conversions, serialises on the target inode with interruptible waiting, clears setuid and related privilege for non directories, asks security policy using filesystem identities, applies changes through the common change path with delegation awareness, waits and retries when a delegation is reported, and finally releases the inode serialisation.

Shared mode update holds a write reference on the mount, serialises on the inode with interruptible waiting, consults security policy, merges caller permission bits with existing non permission bits, marks mode and time for update, applies through the common change path with delegation awareness, retries after waiting on delegation, and releases inode serialisation and mount hold.

Attribute retrieval first asks security policy then fills caller storage. The filling step clears output, advertises basic result coverage, narrows synchronisation options, withdraws atime when the filesystem declares no atime, exposes automount and direct access markers with a mask, prefers filesystem specific handling when available else generic filling, and overlays block device parameters for block device results.

File and node creation enforce writable searchable live parents with absent children and mapped identities. Regular creation requires filesystem create support, prepares mode with permission masking and regular type default, checks security, interrupts directory delegations, invokes filesystem creation and notifies on success. General node creation adds privilege checks for device types except whiteouts, requires filesystem mknod support, checks device policy, and supports character block fifo and socket kinds.

Filename oriented node creation validates the requested type, obtains an exclusive negative dentry with parent write held, checks pathname security using umask adjusted mode, selects mount identity, routes regular types to file creation with post creation security handling and other types to node creation with decoded device values, finalises directory state and references, and repeats with revalidation after delegation waits or stale conditions.

Filename oriented hardlink creation validates option flags, supports empty path and link following selections, resolves the source and exclusively creates the destination, requires both ends on one mount, checks link safety policy and pathname security, invokes shared link mechanics, finalises destination state, and repeats with revalidation after delegation waits or stale conditions while always releasing source and destination references.

Hardlink policy and mechanics impose multiple guards. Policy rejects unmapped ownership, respects a global protection control, otherwise permits owner privileged callers or safe regular non setuid non executable setgid readable writable sources and audits denials. Mechanics requires valid parent checks, single filesystem scope, non append only non immutable non directory sources with link support and mapped identity, enforces link count limits and unlinked file rules under inode serialisation, interrupts delegations, clears linkable marking under small lock, and notifies on success.

Creation type validation allows regular character block fifo socket and zero interpreted as regular, forbids directories as privileged failures and rejects unknown types as invalid. Dentry creation auditing records the attempt then rejects existing names, defunct parents and unmapped identities, otherwise demands write and execute access on the parent.

Propagation busyness assessment first rejects mounts with children or excess references, accepts root like mounts with no parent distinction, then walks propagation peers looking up candidates at the same mountpoint while skipping receiver chains, and reports busy if any candidate chain shows outside children or excess references. Helper logic determines receiver relationships through master chains, selects next candidates only for receivers, and compares reference counts against expected thresholds.

Mount identity translation maps mount view identifiers to filesystem view identities. A pass through map returns the input unchanged, an invalid map yields invalid identity, otherwise an upward table lookup occurs and failures yield invalid identity with initial versus non initial filesystem handling for success. Attribute preparation validates kernel identities, marks owner or group for update, records mount view values, and signals failure for invalid inputs.

Root unmount preparation guarantees a read only superblock before returning success. It serialises on the superblock unmount control, and only for writable instances builds a reconfiguration context requesting read only, parses empty monolithic data, attempts reconfiguration, releases the context, and propagates any construction or reconfiguration failure while always releasing serialisation.

Unmount request validation requires mount privilege, a genuinely mounted path, a recognised mount object, absence of locked marking assessed optimistically, and administrator privilege in the filesystem user context when force is requested, returning permission or invalid argument failures as appropriate.

Shrinkable submount reclamation repeatedly scans a mount subtree for removable members. A mount qualifies only when shrinkable marked, not locked, and propagation idle. Leaf candidates are removed with namespace timestamp update and synchronised propagating tree teardown. The scan descends into populated branches and ascends to reconsider parents whose children vanished, stopping only when a full pass makes no progress.
Mount namespace deletion notification in this fragment is an empty inline operation with no state change, no return value and no observable effect.

Path permission evaluation derives mount identity and backing inode then checks the requested mask. Filename creation resolves the parent, interprets directory and revalidation wishes, suppresses creation for trailing separators without directory request, holds mount write, performs the final lookup under directory ordering, and unwinds write and path references on failure. Creation completion ends directory ordering then drops mount write and path references.

Global namespace mutation serialisation uses an exclusive hold on the namespace semaphore via a small inline helper. Superblock reconfiguration for root unmount holds the superblock unmount semaphore exclusively across writability testing and the entire reconfigure sequence, releasing it on all return paths.

Attribute and link mutation serialises on inodes with interruptible waiting and holds mount write across the critical section. Ownership and mode changes lock the target inode while applying updates and release before delegation waiting with retry. Hardlink creation locks the source inode across link count and linkable checks and delegation interruption, using a small spin protection when clearing linkable marking. Creation paths hold mount write from final lookup until completion handling.

Mount linkage observed here connects parents, children, mountpoints, masters and namespaces. Each mount carries a child list node, a children head, a parent pointer, a mountpoint reference, a master pointer for propagation, an overmount marker, a namespace pointer and a flags word in the embedded public mount. Traversal uses the children head and child node, propagation uses master and mountpoint, and reclamation consults flags and namespace.

Path, attribute, status and delegation carriers appear with consistent roles. A path pairs a mount reference with a dentry reference. An attribute set carries validity bits with mode and mount view owner and group plus time marking. A status record carries mode, result coverage, attribute bits and mask. A delegation carrier starts empty, may be filled by change operations, and drives wait and retry decisions.

Submount shrinking follows a depth first walk with descend, resume and ascend phases inside an outer repeat until stable loop. The walk starts at the given parent, descends whenever a shrinkable candidate has children, attempts removal at leaves, records progress, ascends to the parent on level completion and reattempts the parent itself, aborts early with progress indicated when an unmount mark appears, and the outer loop reruns while any removal occurred.

Creation, link and attribute operations share a delegation and staleness retry cycle. Each attempt performs lookup and mutation with an initially empty delegation carrier. If delegation is reported the operation waits and on success repeats from lookup or delegation clearing point. If staleness is reported the operation enables revalidation and repeats. Final status is returned only when neither condition requests another attempt.

Several conditions silently alter control flow and must be handled. An unmount mark on a parent aborts shrinking while still reporting progress. Locked or propagation busy mounts must never be torn down. Reference count comparisons use strict greater than thresholds that differ between top level and chain checks. Overmount links are ignored when deciding whether a chain member disappears. Delegation waits must precede any retry and stale lookups must enable revalidation.

Creation and link paths carry denial and overflow hazards. Protected hardlink mode can turn otherwise valid links into audited permission failures. Unmapped ownership yields overflow or permission failures rather than proceeding. Link count limits yield too many links, unlinked non linkable sources yield missing file, directory sources and missing filesystem operations yield permission failures, and existing names yield already exists.

Mount and superblock control names observed are MNT_SHRINKABLE and MNT_UMOUNT and MNT_LOCKED and MNT_FORCE with teardown selectors UMOUNT_PROPAGATE and UMOUNT_SYNC and superblock selectors SB_RDONLY and SB_NOATIME. The first selects reclamation candidates, the second aborts scans, the third blocks removal, the fourth gates privilege, the teardown pair drives propagating synchronous removal, read only is enforced for root preparation, and no atime withdraws atime reporting.

Lookup permission capability and query names observed include LOOKUP_FOLLOW plus LOOKUP_DIRECTORY plus LOOKUP_CREATE plus LOOKUP_EXCL plus LOOKUP_REVAL with permission marks MAY_EXEC plus MAY_CHDIR plus MAY_ACCESS plus MAY_READ plus MAY_WRITE and privilege marks CAP_SYS_ADMIN plus CAP_SYS_CHROOT plus CAP_MKNOD and query selectors AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW plus AT_EMPTY_PATH plus AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW plus AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT plus AT_STATX_SYNC_TYPE. Lookup marks guide following creation exclusivity and revalidation, permission marks gate directory file and access checks, privilege marks gate force chroot and device creation, and query selectors guide link handling automount suppression and sync narrowing.

File type permission attribute status and error names observed include type selectors S_IFMT with S_IFREG plus S_IFCHR plus S_IFBLK plus S_IFIFO plus S_IFSOCK plus S_IFDIR plus permission coverage S_IALLUGO with S_ISUID plus S_ISGID plus S_IXGRP plus update marks ATTR_MODE plus ATTR_UID plus ATTR_GID plus ATTR_CTIME plus ATTR_KILL_SUID plus ATTR_KILL_PRIV plus status marks STATX_BASIC_STATS plus STATX_ATIME plus STATX_ATTR_AUTOMOUNT plus STATX_ATTR_DAX plus special values WHITEOUT_DEV plus I_LINKABLE plus failures EPERM plus EINVAL plus EEXIST plus ENOENT plus EOVERFLOW plus EACCES plus EXDEV plus EMLINK. Type selectors route creation and validation, permission bits merge and test access, update marks describe ownership mode and privilege drops, status marks describe result coverage, and failures signal distinct denial causes.
